items.title: Fred Moore Interview, 1959-06-19
items.q: Well, I joined Joe Oliver 1929, right here in New York.

ctx.x: Yeah, I know what that stands for.

So when I'm drumming and I think I'm drumming naturally, I ain't doing nothing, but the folks looking at me laughing. So I catch myself and try to straighten up. First thing you know, I'm still drumming, I get right back in that, that funny look again and people look at me, always looking at me, see. When I'm drumming, I call myself drumming natural. So I have them look around there and the people, aren't you going down the road? Laughing and just, I call it Black Down and Joe Giggle.

So I said to myself, well, I don't laugh at nobody but me. I said, you know, I must look mighty funny up there. So I asked, I said, what? I said, every time I look around, I said, what, what, what are you all laughing about?

items.title: Fred Moore Interview, 1959-06-19
items.q: Dave Nelson was King Oliver's right-hand band... he asked me... 'You want to join King Oliver?'... I said, yeah... I brought my drums... My name is Fred Moore. King Oliver, former drummer.

ctx.x: Uh, the girl's name, the girl named Piano Fash. Used to tell what New York was, the old lady New York was the violin player. I can't remember the name. Jerry Smith? Jerry Smith, yeah, she was on the piano. And, uh, I was playing the clarinet and I was on drums. They're trio trio. He used to play a number like the roses reading them, you know. And, uh, anyway. So we rehearsed this act. About a couple of months we got it together. And, uh, we was booked in this, uh, July 5th theater. For a week. But we stayed two…
Can you explain that first and second ending to me?
